entities.summary:
August Wilhelm Antonius Graf Neidhardt von Gneisenau was a Prussian field marshal who played a crucial role in the reform of the Prussian military during the Napoleonic Wars. His efforts led to the development of the Prussian corps system, which became a model for military organization in Europe.

Gneisenau was a key figure in the War of Liberation against Napoleon's forces, leading the Prussian army to victory at the Battle of Dennewitz in 1813. His leadership and strategic thinking were instrumental in the ultimate defeat of Napoleon at the Battle of Leipzig.

Despite his military successes, Gneisenau's legacy extends beyond the battlefield. He was a prominent advocate for education and cultural development, and his efforts helped to establish the University of Berlin as a center of learning and intellectual inquiry.

In conclusion, August Wilhelm Antonius Graf Neidhardt von Gneisenau was a pivotal figure in Prussian history, whose contributions to military reform and cultural development continue to shape our understanding of the period.
